title: FIX-02 F4 TOCTOU in the set_input_files call path; recording-lookup session test; pid-only snapshot routing and the (pid, xid) side index; discriminating W2c/W2d variants

provider.name: TypeSafe
provider.use: none: every browser cell is a direct MCP caller, no chooser, no model; a socket guard refuses and counts non-loopback connects

hypotheses.A: On F' the isConnected check and DOM.setFileInputFiles are separate CDP commands. A page that detaches/replaces the input inside that window gets the files assigned to the detached node and F' reports success. F5 (same call path) never reports success for a detached node: it refuses or reports unknown.
hypotheses.B: A capture published for session A (publish_capture_for_session) is not resolvable by the recording element lookup running as session B, and is resolvable as A.
hypotheses.C: Neither the pid-only window_for_snapshot routing nor the process-global (pid, xid) side index lets session B's call cause a side effect on session A's window.
hypotheses.D: W2c/W2d can be made discriminating: U' accepts and F5 refuses.

Builds and unit runs take only the cargo lock; never one lock while waiting on the other.

A1.forced_path: Driver env CUA_DRIVER_EXP_SET_FILES_GAP_MS=50; the harness releases the page re-render when the Driver's stderr seam marker appears (after the connectedness check, before the assignment); the page replaces the input (generation 0 -> 1).
A1.oracle: fixture server journal: page beacons of input/change events and of the generation-0 node's files poll, keyed by node generation (old = gen0, fresh = gen1), plus the re-render beacon; page-clock order proves the detach preceded the assignment
A1.race_forced: first seam marker inside the first set_input_files call, re-render released and acknowledged, and on the page clock the re-render precedes every gen0 file event (or there is none)
A1.positive_control: FS: success receipt (status ok) for a race_forced cell in >= 18/20
A1.gate_F5: 0/20 success receipts; 20/20 first calls refused (pre-check browser_ref_stale, or post-assignment browser_ref_stale with detail delivery=unknown, retryable=false); 0 gen0 change events reaching the server in 20/20 cells
A1.prediction_from_source: the last clause FAILS on F5: CDP runs the check and DOM.setFileInputFiles as separate renderer tasks and Chromium fires input/change on the detached node, so F5 can only make the receipt honest (unknown), not prevent the old-node effect => IRREDUCIBLE-with-honest-unknown

A2.gate: after the refusal, one fresh observation, the fresh (gen1) ref set: gen1 change with a file journaled, 20/20 verified (FS reported descriptively)

A3.gate: no seam variable, no re-render: 20/20 verified per arm (gen0 change1 journaled, 0 seam markers, 0 re-render); receipt key set and (status, frame, file_count) identical across all 40 cells

steps.s1: B click {pid, snapshot_id: sA, element_token: tB2} (the spec row)
steps.s2: B bring_to_front {pid, snapshot_id: sA} (routing reader input)
steps.s5: A bring_to_front {pid, window_id: w1} (X RECORD oracle control)

WR.oracle: fixture state file (per-window agreed) before/after each call; X RECORD on the private display: within each step's [send, settled] window, any SendEvent _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW for w1, SetInputFocus to w1, ConfigureWindow with stack mode on w1 or its frame, or FocusIn on w1, its frame or its children counts as a routing side effect on A's window
WR.gate_F_and_F5: s1 and s2 refused 20/20 with 0 mutations and 0 w1 side effects; s3 refused 20/20 (stale_element_token at the F1 filter) with 0 mutations; s4 and s6 verified 20/20; s5 w1 activation observed >= 18/20 (oracle control)
WR.note: spec wording 'refused at the F1 token filter' applies to s3; s1/s2 are expected to be refused earlier, at the registry's closed-schema check (unknown argument snapshot_id), on every arm. U' is reported as is (s3 expected to land, as W2a)
WR.if_F_shows_side_effect: C = REVISE; the routing session check (draft ea12e6f86) is a follow-up, not in F5

WS.steps: A observes w1, B observes w2 (order alternates); B type_text own w2 Note token 'fix03B'; A type_text own w1 Note token 'fix03A'
WS.oracle: fixture state file per-window note_text (CUA_GTK3_NOTE_TEXT_STATE=1, packet fixture copy, two-window mode only)
WS.gate_F5: B's text in w2 and not in w1 20/20; A's text in w1 and not in w2 20/20 (0 cross-window / cross-session writes)
WS.U_and_F: reported as is; a write into the other session's window is an E4 cross-session mutation for that arm

WK.steps: as WS with press_key 'space' delivery_mode foreground on each session's own checkbox token
WK.gate_F5: B toggles w2 only 20/20; A toggles w1 only 20/20

W2dX.steps: A observes w1 and w2; harness closes w1 (SIGUSR1, confirmed); B clicks A's w2 token; A clicks its own w2 token
W2dX.gating_rule: gating (discriminating) only if U' lands B's call >= 18/20 AND F5 refuses 20/20 with 0 mutations AND A's tail verifies 20/20 on F5; otherwise non-gating
W2dX.note: discrimination comes from F1 (session filter), not from window lifecycle: W2d proper (A's closed-w1 token) is refused on U' by AT-SPI object liveness (impl_.rs CachedElementGone), which FIX-02 does not change

W2cX.steps: A and B observe w2; B clicks w2's checkbox point with A's w2 capture; B's own capture at the same point
W2cX.prediction_from_source: non-discriminating by construction: capture admission (capture_registry.rs:842-847 on U') binds runtime generation + session id + session generation and target before FIX-02; F' changes no capture file

e4_counters_per_arm.stale_dispatch: an effect journaled on a node/element that was detached or retired when the effect landed (A1: gen0 file events after the re-render)
e4_counters_per_arm.cross_session_mutation: a fixture-state change on the window of the session that did not send the call (WR s1-s3 on w1; WS/WK B-step change on w1 or A-step change on w2; W2dX/W2cX B-step landing)
e4_counters_per_arm.duplicate: more than one journaled application for one intended action
e4_counters_per_arm.unverified_success: a success receipt (status ok / no refusal) whose intended effect is not independently verified on the intended target (A1: success for a detached node)
e4_counters_per_arm.blind_replay: a re-dispatch after a may-have-landed refusal (the harness never re-dispatches; Driver-internal retries would show as duplicates)
e4_counters_per_arm.refusal_as_success: a refusal receipt while the oracle shows the intended effect landed on the intended target

e4_gate: F5 E4 = 0 on every counter in every row, EXCEPT the A1 stale_dispatch residue which is reported separately as the seam-forced IRREDUCIBLE residue; E4 strict (including it) is also reported

dispositions.F4: KEEP if A1 gate passes and the FS positive control reproduces; REVISE (IRREDUCIBLE-with-honest-unknown, measured claim) if F5 has 0 success receipts and every first call refused/unknown but gen0 events still reach the server; REVISE if the positive control does not reproduce
dispositions.B: KEEP if red on U' and green on F5; REVISE otherwise
dispositions.C: KEEP if WR gates hold on F' and F5 and WS/WK gates hold on F5; REVISE otherwise (routing and side index reported separately)
dispositions.D: each of W2dX, W2cX: discriminating KEEP if its gating rule holds, else non-gating with the SOURCE reason; W2c/W2d proper: non-discriminating by construction
dispositions.regression: 0 failures on F5 suites or the lane reports REVISE
